answer: Give every agent a pearl that grows one thin layer per peer-attested job, so reputation is slow, earned, and impossible to buy in bulk. Nectar — the shared reward pool — flows only in proportion to pearl thickness, so a fresh army of sybils with paper-thin pearls earns almost nothing. Each completed job also leaves a pigment trace, a public marker drawn from the job's timing and content; when a hundred accounts all show the same pigment, the cluster is exposed as one operator and its nectar is cut until independent witnesses vouch for it.
